title: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon
hook: young Yusuf dreams they bow to him, and his father Ya'qub tells him to keep it to himself
carry: not every dream is for telling

segments.voice: Yesterday: 'ijl, the calf made while people said they were waiting for Musa. Your line was wait for the one who's coming back. Today, a new story, told in full.
screen: `WAIT FOR THE ONE WHO'S COMING BACK.`

segments.voice: A boy wakes up and runs to tell his father about a dream. Almost everything we've heard about Ibrahim and Musa, the Qur'an tells in pieces, scattered across many surahs; you gather it up like shells on a beach. Yusuf's story is different. The Qur'an tells it start to finish, in order, in the surah named for him, and at the start it calls what follows the best of stories. For the next two weeks, we'll walk through it in order.
screen: `A BOY AND A DREAM.` → `ONE SURAH, START TO FINISH.` → `THE BEST OF STORIES.`

segments.voice: Surah Yusuf, verse four. Yusuf says: my father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon. I saw them bowing down to me. The Arabic for star, kawkab, can also mean a planet, and some older translations say eleven planets. Either way, the sky is kneeling to a boy. Commentators read the eleven stars as his eleven brothers, and the sun and the moon as his father and mother. It will take years, and a whole surah, to come true. Keep it in your pocket. Now Ya'qub, his father, a prophet himself. He doesn't laugh it off, and he doesn't tell the whole family at dinner. He says: my son, don't tell your dream to your brothers, or they'll plot against you. Satan is a clear enemy to people. He knows his sons, and the jealousy already simmering. So his first gift to Yusuf is discretion: some good things are safer kept close for a while. Then the hope: your Lord will choose you, and teach you the meaning of events, and complete His favor on you, as He completed it on your forefathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq. There's Ibrahim, from earlier on our path, standing in the family line. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave similar advice in a hadith: a good dream is from Allah, and you should tell it only to someone who loves you. Not every dream is for telling. And not everyone who hears it will be glad.
screen: `ELEVEN STARS, THE SUN AND MOON.` · `BROTHERS, FATHER, MOTHER.` · `DON'T TELL YOUR BROTHERS.` · `YOUR LORD WILL CHOOSE YOU.` · then, large: `NOT EVERY DREAM IS FOR TELLING.`

segments.voice: Think of something good happening for you right now, a hope, a small win, a plan just starting, the kind of thing you'd normally post or mention at dinner. Hold it in your mind like a folded note in a pocket, and feel what it's like to keep it just for you: not out of fear, out of care, the way Ya'qub cared for his son. If you pray, you can give thanks for it quietly.
Eleven stars. The boy Yusuf's dream: eleven stars, the sun and the moon, bowing to him, and a father who said, keep it to yourself. Today's word.
Your line: not every dream is for telling. Ya'qub's first gift to his son was a quiet one. Fifty-five days in.

howItsDone: Surah Yusuf is recited and taught as one continuous story, and Muslims who follow the prophetic advice share a good dream only with someone who loves them.

original.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:4: "eleven stars" — kawkab is a star or a planet.

trapdoor: what you thought: a boy with a big ego.
what it means: a boy's true dream, and a wise father who tells him to keep it from brothers who might plot against him.
what a scholar hears: 12:3 calls this ahsan al-qasas, the best of stories, and the surah then tells Yusuf's story in order, start to finish.

notes: 12:4–6 paraphrased, not quoted. 'Some older translations say eleven planets' refers to Pickthall and others; not quoted.
Surah Yusuf has 111 verses; stated. 'The one story the Qur'an tells all at once' is a common description; confirm phrasing.
Interpretation of the eleven stars (brothers) and sun and moon (father and mother; some commentators say father and maternal aunt) given as 'Muslim commentators read it this way'. Confirm.
Hadith on good dreams (Muslim 2261; Bukhari 7044) cited from memory; the 'tell only one who loves you' wording appears in some narrations. Confirm.
